newsitem.title: USA: Brooklyn Union plans $125 mln refunding on Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: Brooklyn Union plans $125 mln refunding on Jan 17.

text.p: Brooklyn Union said on Thursday that it planned to sell on January 17 a total of $125 million of tax-exempt, floating-rate bonds in a refunding that was approved by the state Public Authorities Control Board.
"We're going to call it on January 17," said a company spokesman.
Bart Coleman, manger of financial management, said that the syndicate will be led by Lehman Brothers, adding the team incudes Merrill Lynch, Artemis Capital and Citicorp.

The company decided to issue floaters, whose rate will be reset weekly at market rates, because it determined this strategy should achieve substantial savings. At current rates, floaters would pay around 400 basis points less than the bonds that are being retired, which were sold in December, 1985, Coleman said.
The new bonds will be issued by the New York State Energy Research and Development authority, a state agency.
